problems.title: Evaluate the printed arithmetic literally
problems.question: Evaluate $3.8\cdot5.99-3.7\cdot7.3\cdot16+4.01\cdot3.8-3.7\cdot2.3$.
problems.idea: Group terms that share a factor, keeping the printed factor 16.
formulas: Multiplication is performed before addition and subtraction.
steps: The two terms with factor 3.8 give 3.8(5.99+4.01)=3.8·10=38.
problems.note: The source visibly includes multiplication by 16. None of its choices equals the literal result; the printed exercise appears to contain an error.

problems.title: What two rays can have in common
problems.question: Which cannot be the intersection of two rays: a point, a segment, a ray, a whole line, or the empty set?
problems.idea: An intersection lies inside each original ray.
formulas: A ray starts at one endpoint and extends infinitely in only one direction.
steps: Identical rays intersect in a ray; opposite-facing rays on one line can overlap in a segment or a point.
Disjoint rays give an empty intersection.
A whole line extends indefinitely in both directions, so it cannot be contained in either ray.

problems.title: Remove the teacher from an average
problems.question: The average age of 25 pupils and their 43-year-old teacher is 18. Find the pupils’ average age.
problems.idea: Convert the average to a total, remove the teacher, then divide by 25.
steps: There are 26 people, with total age 26·18=468.

problems.title: Use the repeating last digits
problems.question: Find the units digit of $333^{444}+555^{666}$.
problems.idea: Only the units digit of each base matters.
formulas: The units digits of powers of 3 cycle 3,9,7,1; positive powers of 5 end in 5.
steps: 444 is divisible by 4, so 333⁴⁴⁴ ends in 1.

problems.title: Clear a mixed-number denominator
problems.question: If $\dfrac{0.2X}{3\frac15-1\frac56}=2$, find $X+\frac13$.
problems.idea: Change the mixed numbers to improper fractions.

problems.title: Double a remainder
problems.question: A leaves remainder 15 when divided by 18. What remainder does 2A leave?
problems.idea: Write A as a multiple of 18 plus 15.
steps: The final remainder must be below 18, so it is 12 rather than 30.

problems.title: Divisibility by twelve
problems.question: Replace the final digit in 5835* so the number is divisible by 12.
problems.idea: A number is divisible by 12 exactly when it is divisible by both 3 and 4.
formulas: Divisibility by 3 uses the digit sum; by 4 uses the final two digits.
steps: The digit sum is 21+d, so d is 0,3,6,or9.
The final two digits 50+d must be divisible by 4; among those candidates, only 56 works.

problems.title: Count divisors from prime exponents
problems.question: How many positive divisors does $32\cdot81\cdot25$ have?
problems.idea: Choose independently how many copies of each prime appear in a divisor.
steps: A divisor uses 0 through 5 copies of 2, 0 through 4 of 3, and 0 through 2 of 5.

problems.title: Count a union after removing elements
problems.question: A={3,6,9,12,15,18}; B is the positive even integers below 30; C is the two-digit positive integers ending in 2. Find the size of A∪(B∖C).
problems.idea: First remove C from B, then add only new elements of A.
steps: Its elements in C are 12 and 22, so B∖C has 12 elements.

problems.title: An equation with a custom operation
problems.question: Define a*b=2a+b. Solve the printed equation 3*x=2+x.
problems.idea: Replace the star by its definition before solving.
steps: Subtracting x from both sides gives 6=2.
This is impossible for every x.
problems.note: The printed choices include 6, but no listed number satisfies the equation as written.

problems.title: Count proper fractions
problems.question: For how many positive integers m is $(199-m)/(m+99)$ a proper positive fraction?
problems.idea: Require the numerator to be positive and smaller than the denominator.
steps: The proper-fraction condition gives 199-m<m+99, so 100<2m and m≥51.

problems.title: Subtract before finding the remainder
problems.question: Find the remainder on division by 8 of a=2·3·4·5·7-5.
problems.idea: The product already contains a factor 8.
formulas: If N is divisible by 8, then N-5 has the same remainder as -5.
steps: The factors 2 and 4 multiply to 8, so the product is a multiple of 8.

problems.title: Choose three distinct elements
problems.question: How many three-element subsets does {1,7,0,X,5} have?
problems.idea: A set counts distinct values only.
steps: If X differs from 1,7,0,5, there are five elements. Choose three: 5·4·3/(3·2·1)=10.
If X equals one of the other values, there are only four distinct elements, giving 4·3·2/(3·2·1)=4.
The usual intended answer assumes all five displayed elements are distinct.
problems.answer: 10 if the five elements are distinct; otherwise 4.
problems.note: The statement does not specify X. Its highlighted answer 5 is correct under neither interpretation.

problems.title: Combine a least common multiple and a greatest common divisor
problems.question: Find LCM(45,54)+GCD(36,63).
problems.idea: Use prime factors to find each quantity.
formulas: LCM uses the greatest prime exponents; GCD uses the least shared exponents.

problems.title: Mode, median and mean
problems.question: For 3,7,9,1,3,5,3,1,4,4, find mode+median-mean.
problems.idea: Sort the data and compute each statistic separately.
formulas: Mean=sum/count; for an even count, median=average of the two middle values.
steps: The sorted list is 1,1,3,3,3,4,4,5,7,9. The most frequent value is 3.
The middle values are 3 and 4, so the median is 3.5.

problems.title: Two possible orders on a line
problems.question: A,B,C are collinear, AB=7 and BC=9. Which listed value can AC have?
problems.idea: Consider whether B lies between A and C.
formulas: For three collinear points, the outer distance is the sum of the two inner distances.
steps: If B is between A and C, then AC=7+9=16.
If A and C are on the same side of B, then AC=9-7=2.
problems.answer: AC can be 2 or 16; select 2 from the choices.

problems.title: Match two ratios
problems.question: M,N,K,Q lie in that order. MN:NK=1:2, NK:KQ=3:4, and MK=9. Find MQ.
problems.idea: Use the first ratio to split MK, then the second to find KQ.
formulas: A ratio u:v partitions a total T into Tu/(u+v), Tv/(u+v).
steps: MK=MN+NK=9; the ratio 1:2 gives MN=3 and NK=6.

problems.title: Every pair gives one segment
problems.question: Ten distinct points lie on a line. How many segments have endpoints among them?
problems.idea: Choose the two endpoints without ordering them.
steps: There are 10 choices for the first endpoint and 9 for the second.
This counts each segment twice because AB and BA are the same segment.

problems.title: A bisector next to a larger angle
problems.question: Adjacent supplementary angles AOB and BOC satisfy AOB=3·BOC. Find the angle between OA and the bisector of BOC.
problems.idea: Find both angles, then add half of the smaller one.
formulas: Supplementary angles sum to 180°; a bisector divides an angle equally.
steps: AOB=135° and half of BOC is 22.5°.

problems.title: Distance between two midpoints
problems.question: On a ray from K, KA=30 and KB=40. Find the distance between the midpoints of AB and KA.
problems.idea: Place K at coordinate zero.
formulas: The midpoint of coordinates u,v is (u+v)/2.
steps: The midpoint of AB is 35; the midpoint of KA is 15.

problems.title: Difference of supplementary angles
problems.question: Adjacent supplementary angles α,β satisfy α/5=β/4. Find their difference.
problems.idea: The equal quotients give the ratio 5:4.

problems.title: Lines through points on a circle
problems.question: Seven distinct points lie on a circle. How many different lines join pairs of them?
problems.idea: A line meets a circle in at most two points, so every pair gives a new line.
steps: Choose two of the seven points.
No three of the circle points can lie on one line.

problems.title: Read the possible arrangement of three rays
problems.question: Angles COD=125° and DOB=70°. Find angle COB.
problems.idea: Whether OB and OC lie on the same side of OD affects the answer.
formulas: Angles add for nonoverlapping sectors; the smaller angle corresponding to a reflex angle θ is 360°-θ.
steps: If OB and OC are on opposite sides of OD, the sector through OD is 125°+70°=195°.
Its smaller angle is 360°-195°=165°, the listed intended value.
If both rays lie on the same side of OD, the difference is 125°-70°=55°.
problems.answer: 165° for the intended opposite-side arrangement; 55° is also possible without an arrangement condition.
problems.note: The source supplies no diagram or side condition to make the answer unique.

problems.title: Bisectors of supplementary angles
problems.question: Find the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent supplementary angles.
problems.idea: Each original angle contributes half of itself.
steps: Let the adjacent angles be α and β.
The sector between their internal bisectors consists of half of each angle.
problems.note: The highlighted 30° in the source is incorrect.

problems.title: Maximum intersections of six lines
problems.question: What is the greatest number of intersection points of six lines?
problems.idea: Make every pair intersect at its own point.
steps: Two lines give at most one intersection.
Choose lines with no parallels and no three passing through one point.
All 6·5/2=15 pairs then give different intersections.
